h1: The 5 Best Document Scanners for Computers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Scanners for Computers: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five document scanners for Windows, Mac and Linux computers, compared on drivers, software bundles, duplex and feeder size.
summary: The Epson Workforce ES-400 II is the best fit for a PC-connected desk, with a TWAIN driver and the ScanSmart software suite. The ScanSnap iX2400 offers wired reliability and a 100-sheet feeder, the Brother DS-740D adds duplex to broad driver support, the DS-640 is the cheap multi-OS pick, and the Canon R10 needs no installation.
intro: Scanner reviews rarely mention that the biggest headache is the computer side: a driver that will not install, or software that fights your operating system. Compatibility is a bigger risk than speed.

We reviewed eight scanners on paper, comparing drivers, bundled software, feeder size and duplex support from the listing data, and ranked the five that best cover Windows, Mac and Linux setups. Prices appear as buckets.

products.name: Epson Workforce ES-400 II High-Speed Color Duplex Desktop Document Scanner
products.verdict: A TWAIN driver and full software suite behind a 50-sheet duplex feeder.
products.description:
The ES-400 II pairs a TWAIN driver with the full ScanSmart software suite, a 50-sheet duplex feeder, searchable PDF OCR and Word or Excel conversion. Auto crop and blank-page removal are included.

It wins here because the software side is the most complete in the group, which is what matters when the scanner hangs off a computer. Against the ScanSnap iX2400 it has a smaller feeder but more output conversions.

It suits a PC where scans feed into document tools. Expect to pay more than for the Brother models, since it lands in the $200-500 range.
products.idealFor: A desktop PC feeding scans into document tools.
products.skipIf: You only scan a few pages a week.

products.name: ScanSnap iX2400 High-Speed One-Touch Button Color Document Scanner
products.verdict: Wired USB, a 100-sheet feeder and one-touch scanning.
products.description:
The iX2400 connects over wired USB, which avoids wireless driver complexity, and ships with the ScanSnap Home all-in-one software. It has a 100-sheet feeder and one-touch scan with drag-and-drop to apps.

It ranks second because the software is unified but proprietary, whereas the Epson offers a standard TWAIN driver. In exchange you get twice the feeder capacity.

It suits a desk where the computer stays nearby. The caveat is no wireless option.
products.idealFor: A desk with the computer within cable reach.
products.skipIf: You want a standard TWAIN driver.

products.name: Brother DS-740D Duplex Compact Mobile Document Scanner
products.verdict: Broad driver support plus duplex in a compact body.
products.description:
The DS-740D supports TWAIN and WIA on PC, ICA on Mac and SANE on Linux. It scans duplex, comes with the free iPrint&Scan desktop app and has a desk-saving design.

It ranks third because it takes the DS-640's driver coverage and adds duplex, but the compact build means a smaller feed than the Epson or ScanSnap. It stays in the $100-200 bucket.

It suits mixed Windows, Mac and Linux households. The caveat is that no feeder size is listed.

products.name: Canon imageFORMULA R10 Portable Document Scanner, USB Powered, Duplex
products.verdict: Built-in software means nothing to install.
products.description:
The Canon R10 is a USB-powered portable duplex scanner with a 20-sheet feeder. Its software is built in with no separate installation, updates automatically and works with Windows and Mac.

It ranks fourth because 20 sheets is the smallest feeder here, but it avoids the driver friction that stalls many setups. It sits in the $100-200 bucket.

It suits a laptop user who wants to plug in and scan. The caveat is Linux support is not listed.
products.skipIf: You scan big stacks or use Linux.

products.name: Brother DS-640 Compact Mobile Document Scanner
products.verdict: The broadest driver list at a low price, but single-sided.
products.description:
The DS-640 supports TWAIN and WIA on PC, ICA on Mac and SANE on Linux, with image optimization, bundled OCR software and a free iPrint&Scan desktop app.

It ranks last because the DS-740D adds duplex at the same price bucket, which makes the DS-640 the slower choice for double-sided paper. Both share driver coverage.

It suits a mixed OS home needing occasional scans. The caveat is that duplex is not listed.
products.idealFor: Occasional scans on a mixed OS setup.

whatMatters.detail: TWAIN and WIA are Windows scanner standards, ICA is Mac and SANE is Linux. A scanner that lists all four works across systems. Look for the driver list in the specs.
Bundled software handles OCR, PDF creation and cloud sending. A richer suite saves buying separate tools. Check the listing for OCR and conversion features.
Built-in software avoids installs, but proprietary suites may limit choice. Decide whether you want convenience or a standard driver.
A feeder holds the stack and duplex scans both sides. Both matter if you scan more than a few pages. Find feeder capacity in the title or bullets.
USB powered scanners avoid a wall adapter, and wired connections avoid wireless drops. Check whether the listing says USB powered or wired USB.

faq.a: The Brother DS-640 and DS-740D list SANE driver support. The others do not list Linux.

faq.q: Do I need to install software?
faq.a: The Canon R10 has built-in software with nothing to install. The Epson and ScanSnap use their own suites.

faq.q: Is the DS-740D worth it over the DS-640?
faq.a: If you scan double-sided paper, yes, since it adds duplex. Both share the same driver list and price bucket.
A common scanner driver standard that many apps support. The Epson and Brother models list it.

faq.q: Can I scan to Word or Excel?
faq.a: The Epson ES-400 II lists Word and Excel conversion along with searchable PDF OCR.
Wired USB avoids wireless drops. The ScanSnap iX2400 is wired only.

finalTake: For a PC-connected desk the Epson ES-400 II is the best choice, with TWAIN and a full software suite. The ScanSnap iX2400 handles bigger stacks, the Brother DS-740D covers every OS with duplex, and the Canon R10 is the easiest to set up.
